subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to SharePoint file send requests

question: Should MS Teams standardize on a 30-second Graph control-plane deadline and a five-minute-plus-256-KiB/s SharePoint transfer deadline, and which of the two overlapping timeout PRs should establish the shared helper first?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but the cutoff values intentionally trade indefinite hangs for possible delivery failures on slow Microsoft tenants, and two viable PRs currently claim the same helper ownership.

options.title: Land file-consent helper first
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 as the narrower shared-helper owner, then rebase this PR to retain only the SharePoint/Graph path changes and distinct tests.

options.title: Land this PR first
options.body: Accept this PR as the shared-helper owner, then rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 to reuse the helper for file-consent uploads.

options.title: Recalibrate timeout policy
options.body: Pause both PRs until maintainers choose different control-plane or minimum-transfer thresholds and update both branches consistently.

recommendation.title: Land file-consent helper first
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 as the narrower shared-helper owner, then rebase this PR to retain only the SharePoint/Graph path changes and distinct tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This cross-PR operational policy and landing-order choice needs repository-level ownership rather than an automated code repair.
